BURSEVI:v1p346/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346/r2.claim: In the inward reading, transactions mixed with ulterior aims turn away from God and toward falsehood, thereby invalidating acts of devotion; after truth there is only error.
BURSEVI:v1p346/r2.anchor: والإشارة في الآية في المعاملات إذا كانت مشوبة بالأغراض ففيها نوع من الأعراض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r6.claim: “That is God, your true Lord” points to the one possessing the preceding attributes, whose exclusive divinity merits worship, unlike false idols.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r6.anchor: فذلكم إشارة إلى من اختص بالأوصاف السابقة، الحق الثابت الربوبية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r7.claim: “What is beyond truth except error?” functions as a negative assertion and rebuke; truth and error have no middle ground because they are opposites.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r7.anchor: وماذا استفهام معناه النفي، ولذلك دخلت إلا، وصحبه التقرير والتوبيخ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r8.claim: Grammatically, mā and dhā can combine as one interrogative “what,” with “after truth” as predicate; alternatively dhā is relative and its clause predicates mā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r8.anchor: وماذا مبتدأ تركبت ذا مع ما فصار مجموعهما استفهاما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r9.claim: Since God alone has just been shown to possess those attributes, the rebuke asks how people can turn from manifest truth and worship beings sharing none of them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r9.anchor: ثم وبخهم على اتباع الضلال بعد وضوح الحق قال تعالى: فأنى تصرفون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r10.claim: Using this verse to prove that chess is error is unconvincing: the passage concerns belief, unbelief, and worship, not subsidiary practices on which laws and jurists differ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r10.anchor: واستنباط كون الشطرنج ضلالا من قوله: فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r11.speaker: الجبائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r11.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī uses “how are you turned?” against determinists: if God turns unbelievers from belief they should not be blamed, just as a blind person does not say they blinded themself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p52/r11.anchor: وقد تعلق الجبائي بهذه الآية في الرد على المجبرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p53/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p53/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p53/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī connects the decree to the preceding contrast between truth and error or to their being turned away; Ibn ʿAṭiyya compares it with God’s attributes and the people’s chosen course.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p53/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: كذلك مثل ذلك الحق حقت كلمة ربك

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: If the Quraysh recognize God as creator, sustainer, and giver of life and death, they should recognize Him alone as Lord.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: they should also regard him to be their lord.

SULAMI:v1p301#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p301#4/r1.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v1p301#4/r1.claim: The Real is the goal of worship and companion of obedience, witnessed through none other and reached through none other.
SULAMI:v1p301#4/r1.anchor: قال الحسين : الحق هو المقصود إليه بالعبادات والمصحوب إليه بالطاعات

SULAMI:v1p301#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p301#4/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p301#4/r2.claim: A monotheist cannot claim to testify to God's unity through an independent witness; all else is misguidance, beyond which the lost cannot stand or the incapable describe.
SULAMI:v1p301#4/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي : ﴿ فذلكم الله ربكم الحق فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال ﴾ قال : لا يجوز للموحد

SULAMI:v1p301#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p301#4/r3.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v1p301#4/r3.claim: God does not acquire judgments of good or bad from creatures, since He originated them and cannot be affected by what He created.
SULAMI:v1p301#4/r3.anchor: قال الحسين : الحق هو الذي لا يستقبح قبيحا ولا يستحسن حسنا

SULAMI:v1p301#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p301#4/r4.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p301#4/r4.claim: Being turned away means being diverted from the Real to something else.
SULAMI:v1p301#4/r4.anchor: وقيل في قوله ﴿ فأنى تصرفون ﴾ من الحق إلى سواه

FARRA:v1p462/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p462/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p462/r7.claim: The same three grammatical interpretations of الحق apply in فذلكم الله ربكم الحق.
FARRA:v1p462/r7.anchor: وكذلك قوله: فذلكم الله ربكم الحق

NAHHAS:v2p251/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p251/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p251/r9.claim: الحق can take the same three accusative analyses given for verse 30.
NAHHAS:v2p251/r9.anchor: ويجوز نصب الحق على ما تقدم

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1951/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1951/r1.speaker: مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1951/r1.claim: Malik rejects an unspecified matter as contrary to truth, applying the verse that what follows truth is misguidance.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1951/r1.anchor: قلت لمالك بن انس : ماترى في رجل امره يعنيني قال : ليس ذلك من الحق

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1951/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1951/r2.speaker: مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1951/r2.claim: Malik says chess and backgammon players' testimony is unsound because such play is misguidance.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1951/r2.anchor: سئل مالك عن شهادة اللعاب بالشطرنج والنرد اترى شهادته جائزة ؟ فقال : اما من اتى منها فما ارى شهادتهم طائلة يقول الله عز وجل : فماذا بعد الحق الا الضلال

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1951/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1951/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1951/r3.claim: The question كيف means 'how' in the phrase asking how they are turned away.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1951/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس في قوله : اني قال كيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p158/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p158/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p158/r1.claim: The opening fa draws a conclusion from the rebuke in 10:31; the demonstrative gathers God's preceding qualities as grounds for the judgment, while naming Allah clarifies it and exposes the polytheists' error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p158/r1.anchor: واسم الإشارة عائد إلى اسم الجلالة للتنبيه على أن المشار إليه جدير بالحكم الذي سيذكر بعد اسم الإشارة من أجل الأوصاف المتقدمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p158/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p158/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p158/r2.claim: The following question's fa draws an emphatic, reproachful inference from the proof that God is true Lord; ma dha combines an interrogative with a demonstrative, usually for emphasis, though it can be relative elsewhere.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p158/r2.anchor: والفاء في قوله : { فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال } تفريع للاستفهام الإنكاري على الاستنتاج الواقع بعد الدليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p158/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p158/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p158/r3.claim: After means other than what follows when truth is absent; the rhetorical question denies any middle way, so worship attributed to anything but the true Lord is false and aptly called error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p158/r3.anchor: فالمعنى لا يكون إثر انتفاء الحق إلا الضلال إذ لا واسطة بينهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p159/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p159/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p159/r1.claim: The fa in where are you turned adds explicit rebuke after the denial; anna asks metaphorically where the listeners' reasoning leads them, as if they wandered from one false path to another.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p159/r1.anchor: أي أنكم في ضلال وعماية كمن ضل عن الطريق ولا يجد إلا من ينعت له طريقا غير موصلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p159/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p159/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p159/r2.claim: He praises the Quran's way of expressing these meanings as surpassing every explanation in eloquence, brevity, and clarity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p159/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية : وعبارة القرآن في سوق هذه المعاني تفوق كل تفسير براعة وإيجازا ووضوحا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r4.claim: The God with these attributes is the true Lord, deserving worship; associating another with Him is false and astray, and the Qur’an’s concise expression surpasses any commentary in eloquence and clarity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r4.anchor: ربكم الحق أي المستوجب للعبادة والألوهية،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r5.claim: In monotheistic fundamentals no third position lies between truth and error; derivative legal questions differ because people seek rulings through reasoning, and different laws may make one act lawful or forbidden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r5.anchor: وحكمت هذه الآية بأنه ليس بين الحق والضلال منزلة ثالثة في هذه المسألة التي هي توحيد الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r6.claim: A Prophetic saying distinguishes clear lawful and forbidden matters from ambiguous matters between them, illustrating the contrast with legal branches.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r6.anchor: «الحلال بين والحرام بين وبينهما أمور متشابهات»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r7.claim: Fa-annā tuṣrafūn is a reproach equivalent to the question where are you going?
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p117#2/r7.anchor: وقوله: فأنى تصرفون تقرير كما قال فأين تذهبون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p29/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p29/r1.speaker: الخطابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p29/r1.claim: Al-Khattabi defines the Real as that whose existence is established and valid.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p29/r1.anchor: الحق هو المتحقق وجوده وكل شيء صح وجوده وكونه فهو حق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p29/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p29/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p29/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains “how are you turned away?” as asking how reason can turn people toward worshipping what neither provides, gives life, nor causes death.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p29/r2.anchor: كيف تصرف عقولكم إلى عبادة من لا يرزق ولا يحيى ولا يميت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r4.claim: The Creator and controller whom they acknowledge is the true Lord worthy of exclusive worship; every other object of worship is false.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p266#3/r4.anchor: فكل معبود سواه باطل، لا إله إلا هو

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p267/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p267/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p267/r1.claim: Those who know God created, provides for, and governs everything are asked how they can turn from worshiping Him to worshiping anything else.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p267/r1.anchor: عن عبادته إلى عبادة ما سواه، وأنتم تعلمون أنه الرب الذي خلق كل شيء

JISHUMI:v5p3361/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r1.claim: God brings worshippers together with idols, then separates the parties, who disavow one another; idols are also brought to life.
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r1.anchor: وتدل على أنه يجمع بين من عبد غيره وبين معبوده

JISHUMI:v5p3361/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r2.claim: Everyone receives the consequence of good or evil; no manufactured deity can help, harm, avert punishment, or independently intercede with God.
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن كل أحد ينال جزاء ما قدم من خير أو شر

JISHUMI:v5p3361/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r3.claim: Worshipping idols and fabricating claims are human acts, for which people are punished and reproached, against the Compulsionists' account of human acts.
JISHUMI:v5p3361/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن العبادة والافتراء فعلهم؛ لذلك عاقبهم ووبخهم به

JISHUMI:v5p3362/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r1.claim: The questions establish God's unity and resurrection: God sends rain and produces plants, or sends clouds, rain, celestial bodies, and vegetation, as al-Aṣamm explains.
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r1.anchor: ثم قرر تعالى عليهم أدلة التوحيد والبعث

JISHUMI:v5p3362/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r5.claim: The Creator of these things is the true Lord and alone deserves worship; no third rank lies between truth and error, so anything besides divine unity is false.
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r5.anchor: فذلكم الله يعني فاعل هذه الأشياء ربكم خالقكم الحق أي: يحق له العبادة وحده

JISHUMI:v5p3362/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r6.claim: ‘Where are you being turned?’ means ‘where are you going and straying?’ even if nobody literally turns them away.
JISHUMI:v5p3362/r6.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: معناه أين تذهبون وتضلون، وإن لم يكن هناك غيرهم يصرفهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r5.claim: The one with these powers is the true Lord; truth and error have no middle ground, so leaving truth means entering misguidance, shirk, and misery.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r5.anchor: الثابت ربوبيته ثباتا لا ريب فيه لمن حقق النظر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r6.claim: ‘How are you turned away?’ asks how they turn from truth to error and monotheism to association.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p328#2/r6.anchor: عن الحق إلى الضلال ، وعن التوحيد إلى الشرك ، وعن السعادة إلى الشقاء

MUQATIL:10:31-35/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:10:31-35/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:10:31-35/r2.claim: God is the true Lord; after truth only falsehood remains, and His prior decree means rebellious people will not believe.
MUQATIL:10:31-35/r2.anchor: فماذا بعد عبادة الحق والإيمان إلا الباطل، { فأنى تصرفون }

NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#4/r1.claim: The God with such power is the true Lord, whose lordship is certain to anyone who reasons carefully.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ فذلكم الله ﴾ أى من هذه قدرته هو الله ﴿ ربكم الحق ﴾ الثابت ربوبيته ثباتا لا ريب فيه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#4/r2.claim: There is no middle ground between truth and error; whoever leaves truth falls into error.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#4/r2.anchor: أى لا واسطة بين الحق والضلال فمن تخطى الحق وقع في الضلال

NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#4/r3.claim: They are being turned away from truth to error and from monotheism to idolatry.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p127#4/r3.anchor: ﴿ فأنى تصرفون ﴾ عن الحق إلى الضلال وعن التوحيد إلى الشرك

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r1.claim: The one who does these acts is the true Lord, unlike the beings associated with Him; after leaving worship of the true deity, nothing remains but error.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r1.anchor: أي هذا الذي يفعل هذه الأشياء هو ربكم الحق

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r2.claim: Some earlier commentators read the verse as saying that everything after God is error, and restrict its subject to belief and unbelief rather than deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r2.anchor: وقال بعض المتقدمين: ظاهر هذه الآية يدل

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r3.claim: Another view defines unbelief as covering truth and calls anything other than truth error, with the unlawful error and the permissible guidance because God alone permits and forbids; Qurtubi prefers the first interpretation from the preceding argument about God's acts and exclusive right to worship.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r4.claim: The foundational issue of God's oneness has no intermediate status between truth and falsehood; this is unlike derivative legal questions, which concern rulings attached to established things.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r4.anchor: حكمت هذه الآية بأنه ليس بين الحق والباطل منزلة ثالثة في هذه المسألة

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r5.claim: The distinction is illustrated by 5:48's different laws for communities and the hadith that lawful and unlawful are clear while doubtful matters lie between them; those examples concern practical rulings, not the oneness of God.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r6.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r6.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet's night prayer supplication praising God as the truth, calling His promise, word, meeting, Paradise, Hell, Hour, prophets, and Muhammad true.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32/r6.anchor: الثالثة ثبت عن عائشة رضي الله عنها

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r1.claim: “You are the Truth” means the necessarily existent: God's own existence has no prior or subsequent nonexistence, whereas every other existent is preceded by nonexistence, may cease, and depends on a creator.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r1.anchor: أي الواجب الوجود وأصله من حق الشيء أي ثبت ووجب

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r2.claim: Qurtubi calls Labid's line “everything except God is perishing” the truest poetic utterance and links it to 28:88, where everything perishes except God's face.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r2.anchor: ألا كل شيء ما خلا الله باطل

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r3.claim: Truth and misguidance, like truth and falsehood, form the recognized linguistic and legal contrast; 31:30 says God is the Truth and what people invoke besides Him is falsehood.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r3.anchor: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأن ما يدعون من دونه الباطل

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r4.speaker: ابن عرفة
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿArafa defines misguidance in Arabic as taking a route other than the straight course, or losing something.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عرفة: الضلالة عند العرب سلوك غير سبيل القصد

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r5.claim: Misguidance derives from straying from a road's direction and, in legal usage, is especially used for departure from sound belief rather than deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r5.anchor: والضلال حقيقته الذهاب عن الحق أخذ من ضلال الطريق

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r6.claim: Some exegetes take “He found you astray and guided you” as meaning unaware rather than disbelieving, because the Prophet lacked prior knowledge of scripture and faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#2/r6.anchor: ووجدك ضآلا فهدى [الضحى: 7] أي غافلا، في أحد التأويلات

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r1.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r1.claim: Malik interprets “what after truth except error?” as condemning chess and backgammon.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r2.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r2.claim: Malik disliked playing the game of fourteen with one's wife, saying it is not a believer's conduct and citing the verse.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r3.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r3.claim: Malik calls chess bad, false, and one of the vain games, adding that a rational person should be deterred from such play by his beard and gray hair; al-Zuhri likewise calls it false and dislikes it.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r3.anchor: سئل يعني مالكا عن اللعب بالشطرنج فقال: لا خير فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r4.claim: Among Malikis and most jurists, occasional secret chess without gambling at home is excused, but a habitual public player loses reputation and probity and has testimony rejected.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r4.anchor: أن من لم يقامر بها ولعب مع أهله في بيته مستترا به مرة في الشهر أو العام

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r5.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r5.claim: Shafiʿi's school does not reject the testimony of an otherwise upright chess or backgammon player absent foolishness, suspicion, or grave sin; gambling or being known for it does invalidate probity for consuming illicit wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r5.anchor: وأما الشافعي فلا تسقط في مذهب أصحابه شهادة اللاعب بالنرد والشطرنج

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa's school regards chess, backgammon, the game of fourteen, and all amusements as disliked but accepts the testimony of a player whose good deeds outweigh faults if he commits no evident major sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r6.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: يكره اللعب بالشطرنج

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r7.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r7.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi reports the Shafiʿi distinction that chess exercises thought and ingenuity, whereas backgammon is chance-based gambling like divining with arrows.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r7.anchor: قال ابن العربي: قالت الشافعية إن الشطرنج يخالف النرد

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r8.claim: The backgammon and chess pieces are described as made of boxwood and elephant bone; backgammon is also called al-batil, al-kaʿab, al-arn, and nardshir.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#3/r8.anchor: قال علماؤنا: النرد قطع مملوءة من خشب البقس

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r1.claim: Muslim transmits the Prophet's comparison of playing nardshir to dipping one's hand into pork and its blood; scholars explain this as preparing it to eat, which is forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r1.anchor: في صحيح مسلم عن سليمان بن بريدة عن أبيه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r2.claim: A sound hadith from Abu Musa says playing nard disobeys God and His Messenger; Qurtubi reads the prohibition generally, including chess and play without gambling, as the safer position, though one could limit it to gambling in light of early permissions.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r2.anchor: وهو حديث صحيح، وهو يحرم اللعب بالنرد

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله الحليمي
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r3.claim: Al-Halimi cites a report that playing chess is disobedience to God and His Messenger.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله الحليمي في كتاب منهاج الدين:

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r4.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r4.claim: ʿAli rebukes Banu Tamim players for wasting their purpose in life and says he would strike their faces with the pieces were it not that doing so might become customary.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r4.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه أنه مر على مجلس من مجالس بني تميم

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says chess is worse than backgammon.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r5.anchor: وسئل ابن عمر عن الشطرنج فقال: هي شر من النرد

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r6.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r6.claim: Abu Musa al-Ashʿari says only a sinner plays chess.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r6.anchor: وقال أبو موسى الأشعري: لا يلعب بالشطرنج

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r7.claim: Abu Jaʿfar dismisses chess as a Zoroastrian practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r7.anchor: وسئل أبو جعفر عن الشطرنج فقال: دعونا من هذه المجوسية

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r8.claim: A long prophetic report says God despises players of backgammon, chess, walnuts, and dice, and those who watch them lose all good deeds; Qurtubi says these traditions support prohibition even without gambling and had discussed their pairing with wine in al-Maʾida.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r8.anchor: وهذه الآثار كلها تدل على تحريم اللعب بها بلا قمار

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r9.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r9.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi says some Shafiʿis went so far as to recommend chess, playing it in schools or mosques after study and attributing it to early Muslims; Qurtubi rejects these attributions and claims of sharpening intelligence.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r9.anchor: قال ابن العربي في قبسه: وقد جوزه الشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r10.speaker: أبو الفضل عطاء المقدسي
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r10.claim: Abu al-Fadl ʿAtaʾ al-Maqdisi argues that chess teaches warfare; al-Turtushi replies that it spoils war strategy by telling the king to move out of the way when war aims to seize him.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#4/r10.anchor: سمعت الإمام أبا الفضل عطاء المقدسي يقول

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r1.claim: An account of ʿUmar describing chess as a model of war does not prove he permitted idle chess; he said only that a device useful for warfare would be unobjectionable, assuming it served military learning. Reports of companions not forbidding it may reflect the same assumption or lack of the later hadith.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r1.anchor: فقال: لا بأس بما كان من آلة الحرب

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r2.speaker: الحليمي
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r2.claim: Al-Halimi says that once an authenticated report is established, no one has an argument against it; it binds everyone.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r2.anchor: قال الحليمي: وإذا صح الخبر فلا حجة لأحد معه

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar filled in the pits in a children's game called al-kajja and forbade the children from playing it.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r3.anchor: أن عبد الله بن عمر مر بغلمان

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r4.claim: A report cited by al-Harawi from Ibn ʿAbbas says gambling occurs in everything, even children playing al-kajja; Ibn al-Aʿrabi explains it as children rolling a rag into a ball and gambling with it.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r4.anchor: في حديث ابن عباس: في كل شيء قمار

QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r5.claim: The final question asks how people turn their reasoning toward worship of beings that neither provide, give life, nor cause death.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:32#5/r5.anchor: أي كيف تصرفون عقولكم إلى عبادة ما لا يرزق ولا يحيي ولا يميت

RAZI-FULL:v17p71/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p71/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p71/r1.claim: The one with this power and mercy is the true Lord, whose sovereignty is certain; once truth is established, everything opposed to it must be error because contradictions cannot both be true or false.
RAZI-FULL:v17p71/r1.anchor: ومعناه أن من هذه قدرته ورحمته هو { ربكم الحق } الثابت ربوبيته ثباتا لا ريب فيه

RAZI-FULL:v17p71/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p71/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p71/r2.claim: The question “how are you turned away?” asks how people can abandon manifest truth after recognizing it.
RAZI-FULL:v17p71/r2.anchor: والمعنى أنكم لما عرفتم هذا الأمر الواضح الظاهر { فأنى تصرفون } وكيف تستجيزون العدول عن هذا الحق

RAZI-FULL:v17p71/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p71/r3.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v17p71/r3.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues that the question rebuts compulsion: if God turned unbelievers away from faith, He could not ask how they were turned.
RAZI-FULL:v17p71/r3.anchor: واعلم أن الجبائي قد استدل بهذه الآية وقال : هذا يدل على بطلان قول المجبرة أنه تعالى يصرف الكفار عن الإيمان

SAMIN-DURR:10:32/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:32/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:32/r1.claim: ماذا may be one compound word, with interrogative force dominating the demonstrative; the rhetorical question functions as a negation and thus takes إلا.
SAMIN-DURR:10:32/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون " ماذا " كله اسما واحدا لتركبهما، وغلب الاستفهام على اسم الإشارة

SAMIN-DURR:10:32/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:32/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:32/r2.claim: Alternatively ذا is a relative meaning الذي; the interrogative still functions as negation: what follows truth is nothing but error.
SAMIN-DURR:10:32/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون " ذا " موصولا بمعنى الذي، والاستفهام أيضا بمعنى النفي

STUDYQURAN:10:32/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:32/r1.speaker: JJ, Z
STUDYQURAN:10:32/r1.claim: “That is God” affirms the answer to the questions in the preceding verse.
STUDYQURAN:10:32/r1.anchor: That is God is an affirmation of the response provided in v. 31 (JJ, Z)

STUDYQURAN:10:32/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:32/r2.speaker: Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:10:32/r2.claim: “Your true Lord” means that no one who has thought deeply about God can doubt His Lordship.
STUDYQURAN:10:32/r2.anchor: no one who has thought deeply about God can doubt His Lordship (Ṭ, Z)

TAB-FULL:v12p177/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p177/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p177/r1.claim: The one who performs these acts is the true Lord; anything other than truth is misguidance, so worshipping another god is departure from a truth the audience already admits.
TAB-FULL:v12p177/r1.anchor: لا شك فيه. {فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال} [يونس: 32] يقول: فأي شيء سوى الحق إلا الضلال وهو الجور عن قصد السبيل.

TAB-FULL:v12p177/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p177/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p177/r2.claim: The closing question asks how people can be turned away from the guidance and truth they acknowledge toward another path.
TAB-FULL:v12p177/r2.anchor: فأي وجه عن الهدى والحق تصرفون وسواهما تسلكون وأنتم مقرون بأن الذي تصرفون عنه هو الحق

TABATABAI:10:31-32/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r5.claim: The admission entails that God is the true Lord and deserves exclusive worship; if truth and guidance are with Him, worship of other supposed lords is error.
TABATABAI:10:31-32/r5.anchor: فإن الهدى مع الحق لا غير فلا يبقى عند غيره الذي هو الباطل إلا الضلال

TABATABAI:10:32-33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:32-33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:32-33/r1.claim: The phrase compresses paired opposites: beyond truth with guidance lies only falsehood with error.
TABATABAI:10:32-33/r1.anchor: فماذا بعد الحق الذي معه الهدى إلا الباطل الذي معه الضلال

TABATABAI:10:32-33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:32-33/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:10:32-33/r2.claim: Some exegetes call the paired omission an ihtibāk: “falsehood” is omitted after “truth,” and “guidance” after “error”; the author prefers his own explanation.
TABATABAI:10:32-33/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم ان في الآية احتباكا - وهو من المحسنات البديعية -

TABATABAI:10:32-33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:32-33/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:32-33/r3.claim: The author prefers his direct explanation of the concise wording over the alternative rhetorical analysis.

TABATABAI:10:32-33/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:32-33/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:32-33/r4.claim: “How are you turned away?” asks how long they will turn from truth and guidance toward error.
TABATABAI:10:32-33/r4.anchor: إلى متى تصرفون عن الحق الذي معه الهدى إلى الضلال

ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n51/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n51/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n51/r1.claim: Since the audience admits God creates and governs all and is ultimate reality, no other being can share in His divinity, however slightly.
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n51/r1.anchor: He is the One who creates and governs all things and is the Ultimate Reality behind all that exists

ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n52/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n52/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n52/r1.claim: The literal question means “How, then, are you turned away?” from the truth.
ASAD-NOTES:10:31#n52/r1.anchor: "How, then, are you turned away?"-i.e., from the truth

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r1.claim: After the audience admits that only God can do the things just named, they are told that this is their true Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r1.anchor: لا يقدر عليه إلا الله تعالى: وأقروا به قيل لهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r2.claim: The one who does all these things is the truth; the supposed partners possess none of them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r2.anchor: الذي هذا كله فعله هو الحق ليس هؤلاء الذين جعلتم معه شركاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r3.claim: After the truth, the remaining way is their misguidance and the gods they adopted besides God.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r4.claim: After worshipping God, the only alternative is error: worshipping Satan.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r4.anchor: عبادة الله إلا الضلال، يعني عبادة الشيطان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r5.claim: The closing question asks how reason can turn them to worship beings that neither provide nor give life or death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p187/r5.anchor: كيف تصرف عقولكم إلى عبادة مالا يرزق ولا يحيى ولا يميت

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:32-33/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:32-33/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:32-33/r1.claim: The God who does all this is the true Lord, unlike alleged partners; after God’s worship there is only misguidance, meaning Satan’s worship and beings unable to provide, give life, or cause death.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:32-33/r1.anchor: ليس هؤلاء الذين جعلتم معه شركاء

ELMALILI:10:32/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:10:32/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:10:32/r1.claim: The one with these perfect attributes, powers, acts, creation, and command is Allah, the true Lord and sole rightful deity, master and authority over people.
ELMALILI:10:32/r1.anchor: Allah, hak Rabbiniz ulûhiyet münhasıran kendinin hakkı olan tek mâbud, hakikaten ve bi-hakkın mâlikiniz ve veliyyü’l-emriniz

ELMALILI:10:32/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:10:32/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:10:32/r2.claim: There is no middle position between truth and error: whoever crosses beyond truth falls into error, and every creed other than monotheism is misguidance.
ELMALILI:10:32/r2.anchor: hak ile dalâl beyninde vâsıta yoktur. Hakkı tecavüz eden mutlak dalâlete düşmüş bulunur. Hak teâlâ’dan gayrı rab ma‘dûm ve bâtıl

ELMALILI:10:32/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:10:32/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:10:32/r3.claim: The verse challenges how people are turned from truth to error, monotheism to association, and happiness to calamity, asking where they are being led.
ELMALILI:10:32/r3.anchor: Yani haktan dalâle, tevhidden şirke, saadetten nekbete nasıl çevriliyorsunuz? Dalâle sarf olunmaya nasıl râzı oluyorsunuz?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The demonstrative refers to God's acknowledged true attributes; their logical consequence is exclusive lordship, so turning elsewhere after truth is deep error, contrary to reason.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The logical result of this acknowledgement should have been to accept the God Who has these attributes to be their Lord.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r1.claim: فذلكم summarizes the qualities the questioners acknowledged; the grammar may make Allah an adjective and ربكم the predicate, or treat Allah as predicate and ربكم as apposition, while الحق qualifies or further predicates lordship.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r1.anchor: فذلكة تقرر والإشارة إلى المتصف بالصفات السابقة حسبما إعترفوا به

ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r2.claim: After the true Lord, there is only error: abandoning worship of God alone necessarily leads to worship of another, and worship that associates others with Him is not accepted.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r2.anchor: فمن تخطى الحق وهو عبادة الله تعالى وحده لا بد وإن يقع في الضلال

ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r3.claim: One construal takes الحق as worship of God and الضلال as worship of others; another takes الحق as the true Lord and الضلال as idols, with an expanded view covering monotheism and other worship generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالخحق والضلال مايعم التوحيد

ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r4.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r4.claim: Asked about the testimony of habitual chess and backgammon players, Mālik says he doubts their testimony's worth and applies the verse's judgment that all beyond truth is error.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r4.anchor: ويؤيده ماأخرجه ابن أبي حاتم عن أشهب قال : سئل مالك عن شهادة

ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r5.claim: The interrogative in فأنى تصرفون expresses astonishment and denial of their actual turning away; its force exceeds simply denying the act's occurrence.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r5.anchor: فكيف تصرفون عن الحق إلى الضلال والإستفهام إنكاري بمعنى إنكار الواقع

ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r6.claim: The rebuke truly targets the cause of their turning, since on the author's doctrine God is the agent of the act and it would be incoherent to express astonishment at God's own act.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r6.anchor: ولعل ذلك الإنكار والتعجب متوجهان في الحقيقة إلى منشأ الصرف وإلا

ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r7.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r7.claim: The Muʿtazila say the polytheists themselves create and perform their turning from truth; the agent is left unspoken because the act is too shameful to attribute openly to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p111#2/r7.anchor: وذهب المعتزلة أن فاعل الصرف نفسه المشركون فهم الذين صرفوا أنفسهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132#2/r1.claim: The one who does all this is their true Lord; after truth there is only error, so how can they turn away from worshipping Him while acknowledging Him?
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p132#2/r1.anchor: {فذلكم الله ربكم} الذي يفعل هذه الأشياء هو ربكم، {الحق فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال فأنى تصرفون}

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:32/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:32/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:32/r1.claim: God is the true Lord who deserves worship because He created, enlivened, provided for, and governs people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:32/r1.anchor: أي المتولي لهذه الأمور المستحق للعبادة هو ربكم الثابت ربوبيته لأنه الذي أنشأكم وأحياكم ورزقكم ودبر أموركم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:32/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:32/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:32/r2.claim: The rhetorical question denies anything after truth but error; leaving God's worship leads into misguidance, and the final question asks how people turn away.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:32/r2.anchor: استفهام إنكار أي ليس بعد الحق إلا الضلال فمن تخطى الحق الذي هو عبادة الله تعالى وقع في الضلال. { فأنى تصرفون } عن الحق إلى الضلال.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r6.claim: The God whose unique power and actions were listed is the true Lord; true lordship requires all those attributes, which none other possesses.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r6.anchor: أي الثابته ربوبيته ثباتا لا ريب فيه لاجتماع الصفات الماضية له لا لغيره

BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r7.claim: There is no middle position after truth except misguidance, so no rational person should turn from truth to error.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p439/r7.anchor: فغنه لا واسطة بينهما - بما أنبأ عنه إسقاط الجار , ولا يعدل عاقل عن الحق إلى الضلال

DURR-FULL:v4p362/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p362/r2.speaker: مالك بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v4p362/r2.claim: Malik rejects an unspecified disputed matter as not belonging to the truth and cites the claim that everything after truth is error.
DURR-FULL:v4p362/r2.anchor: عن حرملة بن عبد العزيز قال: قلت لمالك بن أنس رضي الله عنه: ما تقول في رجل أمره يقيني قال: ليس ذلك من الحق

DURR-FULL:v4p362/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p362/r3.speaker: مالك بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v4p362/r3.claim: Malik considers habitual backgammon or chess players’ testimony unreliable, citing that what is beyond truth is error.
DURR-FULL:v4p362/r3.anchor: عن أشهب رضي الله عنه قال: سئل مالك عن شهادة اللعاب بالشطرنج والنرد

TABATABAI:2:21-25#15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#15/r1.claim: Truth is one and unified, whereas falsehood is scattered and divisive; therefore true propositions cohere and support one another rather than contradicting one another.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#15/r1.anchor: فقد جعل الحق واحدا لا تفرق فيه ولا تشتت
